moves.label: Close port USLAX (Port of Los Angeles)
moves.rationale: Closing the Port of Los Angeles will disrupt a significant number of exporters and cause a substantial immediate loss.

moves.label: Reroute exports away from port USLAX (Port of Los Angeles)
moves.rationale: Rerouting exports from the closed Port of Los Angeles to other major ports will significantly reduce the current capability loss.

moves.label: Outage at facility FAC02801 (Ulvane Volans Industries Ltd - Barrow)
moves.rationale: Targeting a single point of failure in the deep network will maximize disruption and create lasting pressure.

moves.label: Replace the production of facility FAC02801 (Ulvane Volans Industries Ltd - Barrow)
moves.rationale: Replacing the facility will recover the most significant portion of the lost production capability.

moves.label: Close port USHOU (Port of Houston)
moves.rationale: Targeting the Port of Houston will disrupt a significant number of exporters and add substantial capability loss.

moves.label: Reroute exports away from port USHOU (Port of Houston)
moves.rationale: Rerouting exports from the recently closed Port of Houston will significantly reduce the current capability loss.

moves.label: Block the Dover Strait
moves.rationale: Targeting the Dover Strait will force significant rerouting and add substantial delay, increasing pressure on the supply chain.

moves.label: Harden port USORF (Port of Norfolk)
moves.rationale: Since hardening the Dover Strait is not possible, the next best option is to harden a major port that is likely to be targeted next, such as the Port of Norfolk.
